text: What is a Cybercab? Tesla's two-seat robotaxi, built in Austin, Texas. A Cybercab is a two-seat, self-driving taxi made by Tesla and built at its Gigafactory in Austin, Texas. It has no steering wheel and no pedals, and Tesla intends it for its robotaxi ride service. Musk said Cybertruck production at the Austin plant will wind down around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab production.. Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on a Friday in November 2026 that Cybertruck production in Austin, Texas, will wind down around mid-2027 to free capacity for the Cybercab. The Cybertruck, which had sold about 70,000 units since 2023, will be phased out to make room for the robotaxi.. The Cybercab is designed only for autonomous driving. It has no steering wheel, no pedals, no side mirrors and no rear window. Tesla uses a camera-based driving system on it rather than the lidar and radar that some rival robotaxis carry. Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on a Friday post on X that Cybertruck production at the Texas Gigafactory would wind down around the middle of 2027. The space would then make room for more Cybercab output. The Austin plant also builds the Model Y, and it is the only Tesla factory known to assemble the Cybertruck. Musk has called it a crucial product for the company's future. Its success is not guaranteed: a federal investigation into the vehicle is under way, and Tesla has not yet reached fully self-driving operation after more than 10 years of effort.

Tesla Cybertruck production end: Texas plant winds down mid-2027. Tesla will end Cybertruck production at its Texas Gigafactory in Austin around the middle of 2027, Elon Musk said in a post on X, to free space for the Cybercab robotaxi. The Cybertruck is an electric pickup that Tesla began delivering in late 2023. Musk has not said whether the truck will be built anywhere else.. Musk said in a post on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in Texas around the middle of next year. The factory space will be used to expand Cybercab production.. Musk said the factory would make room for increased Cybercab output, a two-seat vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals. The Cybertruck is built only at this Texas plant, which also makes the Model Y. Tesla also did not say whether the Cybertruck would be discontinued altogether. Sales have been well below early forecasts. Musk predicted 250,000 trucks a year, but analysts estimate roughly 70,000 to 71,000 have been delivered since 2023. Cox Automotive put 2025 US sales at 20,237, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. The cheapest version now lists at $59,900, while the company first promised $39,900. The truck has also faced several recalls, quality complaints, and a federal investigation tied to Tesla's autonomous vehicle work. Its specifications fell short of those Tesla advertised at launch.
